name: Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi Mini Plug-In Switch (D215P)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi per Leviton's guide. The CSA listing shows Wi-Fi and Bluetooth as transports; Bluetooth is likely for setup only.

matter.note: Matter comes with a firmware update in the My Leviton app. CSA lists the D215P (Matter 1.3, firmware 2.3.10, certified 2025-05-20); other CSA pages show a second certificate ID for it.

apple_home.note: Pairs with Apple Home directly through HomeKit, using the HomeKit code that comes with it. The optional Matter update removes the HomeKit link; it must then be re-added with the Matter code, which needs an Apple home hub.

google_home.note: Through the My Leviton cloud link; Matter is also an option after the firmware update.

alexa.note: Through the My Leviton Alexa skill; Matter is also an option after the firmware update.

smartthings.note: Leviton lists SmartThings, and says the Matter update doesn't affect the existing SmartThings integration. Matter is also an option.

home_assistant.note: Through Home Assistant's Matter integration after the Matter firmware update. We found no official Leviton integration for Home Assistant.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; no Leviton hub needed.

localControl.note: With the Matter firmware, Matter controllers reach it on the local Wi-Fi network. Leviton doesn't state local control for its own app.

energyMonitoring.note: Leviton's product page and spec sheet don't mention energy monitoring, but no source says it is absent.

maxLoadWatts.note: Leviton rates it 15 A general use at 120 V, 1500 W incandescent/halogen, 5 A LED/CFL and 3/4 HP motor. It gives no single wattage figure for general use.

summary: The Leviton D215P is a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi mini plug-in switch that needs no hub. Through the My Leviton app it works with Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, and it can join Apple HomeKit directly. A firmware update adds Matter, which also lets Home Assistant control it locally. Leviton rates it 15 A for general use and 1500 W for incandescent lights; energy monitoring isn't listed.
caveats: Matter needs a firmware update from the My Leviton app, and the update removes the existing HomeKit pairing, so you have to re-add it to Apple Home.
Load limits depend on load type: 15 A general use, 1500 W incandescent, 5 A LED/CFL.
